parts.title: Reading - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage_text:
Jimmy is a very special dog. He lives with Sarah and Kevin Ashby and their parents in Cornwall. However, it is surprising that Jimmy is still living in Cornwall after he spent a year having an adventure!

It all started when the family went on holiday. They travelled five hundred miles to Scotland by car from Cornwall with their dog sitting on the back seat with the children. They all had a wonderful time. They walked up mountains and Jimmy loved jumping into the lakes, or 'lochs' as they are called in Scotland. The whole family did everything together.

On the last day, the Ashby family packed their suitcases to go home. When they finished, Jimmy wasn't there. The whole family spent hours trying to find him, but they couldn't. At last it was time to go home. The children were very upset and said they didn't want to leave without Jimmy. The family drove back to Cornwall without their pet. They thought he was lost forever.

For a year, the family were very sad. They hoped someone would find Jimmy. They even thought about getting a new dog, but they knew that no dog would be as good as Jimmy.

A year later Sarah heard a strange noise outside the door of their house. When she opened it she found Jimmy standing there. The whole family cried because everyone was so happy that Jimmy was home. To this day, no one knows what Jimmy did during that year away!

options.A: has lived in Cornwall for a year.
options.B: had a very bad adventure more than one year ago.
options.C: arrived in Cornwall one year ago.

options.A: they searched for him for a long time.
options.C: they decided to stay in Scotland.

questions.question: For a year, the Ashby family

options.B: searched for their dog in Cornwall.

parts.title: Listening - Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one word or a number or a date or a time.
parts.context: You will hear a teacher telling students about a hotel they will stay in during a trip.
parts.transcript:
Good morning boys and girls. Let's have a look at the hotel information for our trip to Edinburgh. When we arrive in town, we'll go straight to St Andrew Square, which is 5 minutes' walk from the railway station and very close to our hotel, the Dork, which is in George Street. Tell your parents that the price for a double room is 120 pounds a night, and a single room is 90 pounds a night. So, if you're sharing a room, the price is 60 pounds a night.
The hotel is very big, there are 100 bedrooms, but we only need 20, possibly on the same floor.
It's a very nice hotel with a lot of facilities, such as a gym, a sauna and even a swimming pool, but we won't have time for any of those, we've got a very busy schedule!
So, did you get the address right? It's George Street, and the hotel is opposite the Post Office.

parts.title: Listening - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear a conversation in a shop.

options.B: the painting is the best present.

questions.question: In the end Kevin decides to

parts.transcript:
Shop assistant: Hello, can I help you?
Kevin: Ah, yes please. I'm looking for a present for my mum. It's her birthday next week.
Shop assistant: Let me see. Ah, here's a very lovely painting. What do you think?
Kevin: I really like the colour but it's too expensive for me. What else have you got?
Shop assistant: I know, how about this old guitar: you can't play it anymore, but it would look very good on the wall in your living room?
Kevin: My mum already has a guitar. She likes old things, you know, like stuff from the past. She thinks modern furniture is horrible!
Shop assistant: Then this Italian glass lamp is the perfect gift! I found it in a shop in Spain last year. It's fifty years old and very special. It still works too.
Kevin: Oh yes. The painting was very beautiful, but this table lamp is the best for Mum!
Shop assistant: Fine. So, that's thirty pounds.
Kevin: Oh, I haven't got the money now. Can you keep the lamp until next week? I'll ask my dad if he can come with me and get it next Tuesday after school.
Shop assistant: No problem, I'll see you next Tuesday.

parts.title: Listening - Part 5
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear two girls talking about another girl. What does she do on each day of the week?
parts.transcript:
Lisa: Hi, Karen, have you seen your sister today?
Karen: Of course I haven't! It's Sunday, and you know my sister always goes ice skating on Sundays!
Lisa: Oh yes. I suppose I'll have to see her tomorrow then.
Karen: What? On Monday? No, she's joined a gym and she goes there every week.
Lisa: How about Tuesday? Do you think she'll be free then?
Karen: Maybe. But she usually goes to play tennis on Tuesdays.
Lisa: Oh yeah. And on Wednesday she has her painting class.
Karen: No, painting is now on Thursday. But you won't see her Wednesday because we're all going out to a restaurant for my dad's birthday.
Lisa: OK, I'll wait until Friday!
Karen: Umm, no, football is on Friday.
Lisa: What? She can't even play football!
Karen: Yeah, I know. But she likes to go and watch. Perhaps you can try and see her next week instead?
